⚡️ First International Festival of Nima Yushij kicks off in Mazandaran

📌 Sari, IRNA — The first International Nima Yushij Festival kicked off at the University of Mazandaran, with articles submitted by researchers from Iran as well as the Caucasus, Central Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.

Speaking on Tuesday, Morteza Mohseni, secretary of the festival, said the event will be underway at the University of Mazandaran until November 26, and that more than 150 articles by researchers from Iran and the countries of the Caucasus region, Central Asia, and the Indian subcontinent have been submitted to the festival secretariat.
​
The event is set to be held across sections including books, poetry, film, podcasts, painting, calligraphy, and a scientific conference, he added.
​
The festival is designed to revisit Nima Yushij’s thought, works, and literary standing, and to examine his impact across scientific, cultural, and artistic fields.
​
The scientific section covers topics such as Nima and cultural studies, Nima and social studies, Nima and artistic studies, Nima and literary studies, Nima and literary criticism, Nima and modern poetry, Nima and classical poetry, Nima and Mazandarani poetry, and Nima and literary schools, Mohseni stated.
​
The cultural and artistic section incorporates various disciplines — including theater, local music, photography, painting, film, and calligraphy — to facilitate a multi-dimensional examination of Nima’s personality and legacy, he said.

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says no negotiations will take place until seven conditions set by Iran are met, stressing that the country is fully prepared to respond decisively to any hostile moves.

Speaking at an open session of Parliament on Tuesday, Ghalibaf said Iran’s position remained clear and unchanged in the face of threats and insults by the US president.
​
The speaker said threats against the Iranian people and renewed emphasis on economic pressure were primarily signs of Washington’s desperation in the face of Iran’s resilient, independent nation.
​
He added that Iran would take no action and enter no negotiations before the implementation of its seven conditions, warning that Tehran was prepared to deliver a decisive response to any hostile moves and expand the geographical scope of the battlefield if its adversaries made a miscalculation.
​
Iran has repeatedly said that its seven conditions must be met before negotiations with Washington can resume. The demands, which have been conveyed through mediators, include an end to hostilities on all fronts, the lifting of US sanctions and its naval blockade of Iranian ports, and the release of frozen Iranian assets.
